_note_2026_09_08_factcheck: 2026-09-08 (vin, claude-code session 30f42822): operator-ordered fact check ('Fact check it') of the Prima trio 19 days before sailing, against primary sources where reachable. MAJOR: the day-by-day had the ports on the wrong days (sea day Mon, cay Tue, sea Wed, Falmouth Thu, Cayman Fri, Cozumel Sat with a 7 PM sail and Port Canaveral at 6:30 the next morning). NCL's published order for this fall's Western sailings, confirmed against the Great Stirrup Cay and Falmouth port schedules, is cay Mon, sea Tue, Falmouth Wed, George Town Thu, Cozumel Fri, sea Sat. All hours corrected. MAJOR: embarkation terminal was given as Cruise Terminal 10; the Port Authority's 2026 master schedule has Prima at CT5 on Sept 27 and CT6 on Oct 4. MAJOR: drink-package math used the pre-2025 $109/day list price; NCL's current terms (Free at Sea back from Nov 5 2025; $45/day + 20% on board) substituted and the budget row cut from $760+ to ~$380. VENUES: The Cavern Club (x2) and Soleil Bistro (x2) are not on Prima; Hudson's is Deck 7 not 8; a bullet claiming Onda by Scarpetta is not aboard contradicted the dining list and was removed. OTHER: NHC peak is Sept 10 (pack called late September the highest-risk week); Dunn's River is ~1 hour from Falmouth, not 2; Vibe '$399 week' unsupported; KSC $77; check-in closes 3 days out not 7; Cayman population restated from the census; the cay was leased in 1977 and bought in 1986; 'NCL for Me app' is not a product name. PIER: the June row's 'reopened by Sept 29' was a forecast; rewritten on the Sept 3 opening coverage (Luna scheduled to dock Sept 4) with the second-berth status stated as unknown. HANDOFF CARD: still carried the NCL Care Team numbers (+1 305 436-4000 / +1 866 234-0292) that the June 11 audit marked unverified and removed from the long form, and omitted the George Town consular agency; aligned to the long form's verified block. NOT CHANGED, flagged: ship page ncl.com shows 3,195 guests vs the pack's 3,099 (double occupancy, Wikipedia); NCL's departure time (4 PM) and the Port Authority's (6 PM) disagree and the pack says so rather than picking one.
